questions.question: Why are autotrophs placed at the first trophic level in the food chain?

options.text: Because they make food from inorganic substances.
Because they consume organic waste as food.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because they make food from inorganic substances**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Autotrophs** are organisms that can produce their own food using light, water, carbon dioxide, or other chemicals; they are essentially the **primary producers** of an ecosystem.

• They utilize **inorganic substances** from the environment, such as **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) and **water** (H₂O), to synthesize **organic molecules** like glucose through the process of **photosynthesis**.

• Because they are the only organisms capable of converting **solar energy** into **chemical energy**, they form the foundation of all **biotic communities**.

• In any **food chain** or **ecological pyramid**, autotrophs are placed at the **first trophic level** because they provide the initial energy source that sustains all other levels.

• Common examples of autotrophs include **vascular plants** on land and **phytoplankton** or **algae** in aquatic environments.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Trophic Levels**: These represent the feeding positions in a food chain, where energy flows from **producers** to various levels of consumers.

• **Herbivores**: These are **primary consumers** that occupy the **second trophic level** because they feed directly on plants.

• **Heterotrophs**: Unlike autotrophs, these organisms cannot manufacture their own food and must rely on the consumption of other organisms for **nutrition**.

• **Decomposers**: Organisms such as **bacteria** and **fungi** that break down dead organic matter and **organic waste**, playing a vital role in **nutrient cycling**.

• **Saprophytes**: A specific group of decomposers that obtain nutrients by absorbing organic matter from decaying organisms through **extracellular digestion**.

• **Energy Flow**: According to **Lindeman's 10 percent law**, only about 10% of the energy available at one trophic level is transferred to the next, which is why **producers** must be the most abundant group.
</ul

questions.question: A 7 { V} battery is connected in series with five resistors: 0.1 Omega , 0.4 Omega , 0.5 Omega , 0.6 Omega and 12.4 Omega . What is the current flowing through the 12.4 Omega resistor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series circuit**, the **total resistance** (also known as equivalent resistance) is the **sum of the individual resistances** connected in the path. The formula used is **Req = R1 + R2 + R3 + R4 + R5**.
 
• For the given problem, the individual resistances are **0.1 Ohm**, **0.4 Ohm**, **0.5 Ohm**, **0.6 Ohm**, and **12.4 Ohm**. Adding these values: **0.1 + 0.4 + 0.5 + 0.6 + 12.4** equals a total resistance of **14.0 Ohm**.
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the relationship between **voltage (V)**, **current (I)**, and **resistance (R)** is given by the formula **V = I x R**. To find the current, we rearrange the formula to **I = V / R**.
 
• Given a **battery** of **7 V** and a total calculated resistance of **14 Ohm**, the total current in the circuit is **7 / 14**, which equals **0.5 A**.
 
• A fundamental characteristic of **series connections** is that the **current remains constant** through every component in the circuit. Therefore, the current flowing through the **12.4 Ohm** resistor is exactly the same as the total circuit current, which is **0.5 A**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 0.5 A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law:** 
 
 
• Discovered by **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, this law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• It is the most basic law of **electricity** and is used to calculate the power, efficiency, and safety of electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Series vs. Parallel Circuits:**
 
 
• In a **series circuit**, components are connected **end-to-end**, creating a **single path** for current. If one component fails, the entire circuit is broken.
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, components are connected across the same two nodes, providing **multiple paths** for current. In this setup, the **voltage remains constant** across all branches, but the current divides.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• **Voltage** is measured in **Volts (V)**, representing the electrical potential difference.
 
• **Current** is measured in **Amperes (A)**, representing the rate of flow of electric charge.
 
• **Resistance** is measured in **Ohms (Ω)**, representing the opposition to the flow of electric current.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Voltage Drop in Series:** While the **current** is the same in a series circuit, the **voltage** is divided among the resistors. The **voltage drop** across the **12.4 Ohm** resistor can be calculated as **V = I x R = 0.5 A x 12.4 Ohm = 6.2 V**.
 
• **Total Resistance Property:** In a **series combination**, the **equivalent resistance** is always **greater** than the largest individual resistance in the circuit (14 Ohm > 12.4 Ohm).
 
• **Application:** Series circuits are often used in simple devices like **flashlights** or **decorative string lights**, though modern string lights often use parallel sections to prevent the entire string from going out if one bulb fails.

questions.question: What property distinguishes a compound from a mixture?

options.text: There is a fixed balance and characteristics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a fixed balance and characteristics**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more chemical elements are **chemically bonded** together. The most defining characteristic of a compound is that the elements are always present in **fixed ratios** by mass.

• This fixed ratio is governed by the **Law of Definite Proportions** (also known as **Proust's Law**), which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.

• Unlike mixtures, the formation of a compound involves a **chemical change**, resulting in a product with **entirely different properties** from its constituent elements. For example, **Sodium** (a reactive metal) and **Chlorine** (a toxic gas) combine to form **Sodium Chloride** (common table salt).

• Compounds possess a **fixed melting and boiling point**, which serves as a benchmark for their **purity**. Because they are held together by chemical bonds (ionic or covalent), they cannot be separated by simple **physical methods** like filtration or evaporation.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Mixtures**:

• Components are physically combined and can be present in **any proportion**.

• They retain the **original properties** of their constituents (e.g., in a mixture of iron and sulfur, iron remains magnetic).

• They can be **homogeneous** (uniform composition like **Alloys**) or **heterogeneous** (non-uniform like **Soil**).

• Separation is possible through **physical processes** such as **distillation**, **sublimation**, or **magnetism**.

• **Separation of Compounds**:

• Compounds can only be broken down into their individual elements through **chemical reactions** or **electrochemical reactions** like **electrolysis**.

• **States of Matter**:

• The option **Always solid** is incorrect because compounds can exist in all three states of matter: **solid** (Calcium Carbonate), **liquid** (Water), and **gas** (Carbon Dioxide).

</ul

questions.question: What does the area under a velocity–time graph represent?

options.text: The displacement of the object during that time interval
The time taken by the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The displacement of the object during that time interval**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **area under a velocity–time (v-t) graph** represents the **displacement** of an object over a specific **time interval**. Since **velocity** is defined as the **rate of change of displacement** ($v = dx/dt$), the integral of velocity over time ($\int v dt$) yields the total **change in position**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• In a graph where the **velocity** is plotted on the **y-axis** and **time** is plotted on the **x-axis**, the product of the two dimensions (**m/s × s**) results in **meters (m)**, which is the **SI unit** for **displacement**.
 
• For an object moving with **uniform velocity**, the graph is a **straight horizontal line**. The area formed under this line up to the **time axis** is a **rectangle**, where the **Area = Velocity × Time**.
 
• If the object moves with **uniform acceleration**, the graph is a **sloping straight line**. The area under this curve (often a **triangle** or a **trapezium**) still represents the **net displacement**.
 
• It is important to note that **displacement** is a **vector quantity**. Therefore, areas above the **time axis** (positive velocity) represent **positive displacement**, while areas below the axis (negative velocity) represent **negative displacement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration:**
 
 
• The **slope (gradient)** of a **velocity-time graph** represents the **acceleration** of the object.
 
• A **steeper slope** indicates a **higher magnitude of acceleration**, while a **zero slope** (horizontal line) indicates **constant velocity** and **zero acceleration**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect as the area does not represent acceleration.***
 
 
 
• **Speed and Distance:**
 
 
• The **area under a speed-time graph** represents the total **distance** traveled, which is a **scalar quantity**.
 
• Unlike displacement, **distance** is always **positive**. To find distance from a velocity-time graph, one must take the **absolute value** of the areas (treating negative areas as positive) and sum them up. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Position-Time Graph:**
 
 
• In a **position-time (s-t) graph**, the **slope** at any point represents the **instantaneous velocity** of the object.
 
• A **curved line** on a position-time graph indicates that the velocity is changing, meaning the object is **accelerating**.
 
 
 
• **Time Taken:**
 
 
• **Time** is represented by the **independent variable** on the **x-axis**. It is not represented by the area but rather by the **interval** along the horizontal axis. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Equations of Motion:** The geometric derivation of the **three equations of motion** ($v = u + at$, $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at²$, and $v² = u² + 2as$) is often performed using the **area and slope properties** of the **velocity-time graph**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** For **non-uniformly accelerated motion**, the velocity-time graph is a **curve**. In such cases, **calculus (integration)** is required to calculate the **area under the curve** to find the **displacement**.
 
• **Directionality:** If an object returns to its **starting point**, the total **area above the x-axis** will equal the total **area below the x-axis**, resulting in a **net displacement of zero**, even though the **distance** traveled is non-zero.

74

questions.question: Which category of sound frequency is used by rhinoceroses, whales, and elephants for communication?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**Infrasound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infrasound** (or infrasonic sound) refers to sound waves with a frequency lower than the lower limit of human audibility, which is generally **20 Hz**.
 
• Large mammals such as **Rhinoceroses**, **Whales**, and **Elephants** utilize infrasound to communicate over vast distances. ***Hence, the correct answer is Infrasound.***
 
• **Rhinoceroses** are known to communicate using infrasound of frequency as low as **5 Hz**.
 
• **Elephants** use low-frequency sounds to coordinate herd movements and find mates over distances of several **kilometers**, as these waves are less likely to be scattered or absorbed by dense vegetation.
 
• **Whales**, specifically **Baleen whales**, use infrasonic calls to communicate across hundreds or even thousands of kilometers in the **ocean**, taking advantage of the efficient propagation of low-frequency waves in water.
 
• Natural events like **earthquakes**, **volcanic eruptions**, and **ocean waves** also generate infrasonic waves, which some animals can perceive as a warning signal before the event occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Audible Sound:**
 
 
• This is the frequency range detectable by the human ear, typically spanning from **20 Hz to 20,000 Hz** (or **20 kHz**).
 
• Sounds below **20 Hz** are felt as vibrations rather than heard, while sounds above **20 kHz** are completely silent to humans.
 
 
 
• **Ultrasound:**
 
 
• Sound waves with frequencies higher than **20,000 Hz** are classified as ultrasound.
 
• Animals like **Bats**, **Dolphins**, and **Porpoises** produce ultrasound for **echolocation** to navigate and hunt prey in the dark or underwater.
 
• In **medical science**, ultrasound is used in **Sonography** (ultrasound imaging) to view internal organs and during **pregnancy** to monitor fetal growth.
 
 
 
• **Supersonic Sound:**
 
 
• The term **Supersonic** does not refer to a frequency range but to a **speed**. It describes an object moving faster than the **speed of sound** in air, which is approximately **343 meters per second** (at **20 degrees Celsius**).
 
• When an aircraft travels at supersonic speeds, it creates **shock waves** known as a **sonic boom**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sound Propagation:** Sound is a **mechanical longitudinal wave** that requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot travel through a **vacuum**.
 
• **Frequency and Pitch:** The **frequency** of a sound wave determines its **pitch**. High-frequency waves (ultrasound) have a high pitch, while low-frequency waves (infrasound) have a very low pitch.
 
• **Infrasound Detection:** Specialized instruments called **microbarometers** are used to detect and monitor infrasound for **scientific research** and **nuclear explosion** monitoring under the **Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT)**.
 
• **Age and Hearing:** As humans **age**, the upper limit of the **audible range** often decreases, making it harder to hear high-frequency sounds near **15-20 kHz**.
</ul

questions.question: Metals high in the activity series may be extracted by the process of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**electrolytic reduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals high in the activity series, such as **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Aluminium (Al)**, are very reactive and cannot be obtained from their compounds by heating with **carbon**.
 
• This is because these metals have a higher **affinity for oxygen** than carbon does, making carbon an ineffective reducing agent for their oxides.
 
• **Electrolytic reduction** is the process used for their extraction, where **electric current** is passed through the **molten** state of their **chlorides** or **oxides**. ***Hence, the correct answer is electrolytic reduction.***
 
• During this process, the **metal** is deposited at the **cathode** (the **negatively charged electrode**), and the non-metal, like **chlorine**, is liberated at the **anode** (the **positively charged electrode**). *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• **Only heating** is a method used for metals very **low in the activity series**, such as **Mercury** from its ore **Cinnabar (HgS)**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Calcination** is a process used for **carbonate ores** of metals with **medium reactivity**, where the ore is heated strongly in **limited supply of air** to convert it into an oxide. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Heating with carbon** (reduction) is used for metals in the **middle of the activity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, and **Lead (Pb)**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:** It is a vertical arrangement of metals in **decreasing order** of their **chemical reactivity**. Metals at the top are the most **electropositive** and lose electrons easily.
 
• **Extraction of Sodium:** It is obtained by the **electrolysis** of **molten sodium chloride (NaCl)**. At the **cathode**, **Na+** ions gain electrons to form **Sodium metal**, while at the **anode**, **Cl-** ions lose electrons to form **Chlorine gas**.
 
• **Hall-Heroult Process:** This is a specific industrial **electrolytic process** used for the extraction of **Aluminium** from **Alumina (Al2O3)**. The alumina is dissolved in molten **cryolite (Na3AlF6)** to lower the **melting point** and increase **conductivity**.
 
• **Roasting:** Unlike calcination, **roasting** is the process of heating **sulphide ores** strongly in the **presence of excess air** to convert them into **metal oxides**.
 
• **Native State:** Metals at the bottom of the activity series, like **Gold (Au)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Platinum (Pt)**, are often found in their **native (free) state** in nature because they are the **least reactive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Affinity for Oxygen:** The choice of extraction method is primarily determined by the **thermodynamic stability** of the metal oxide. Metals high in the series form **very stable oxides** that require massive energy (electricity) to break.
 
• **Reducing Agents:** While **carbon (coke)** is a cheap and common **reducing agent** for **Iron** and **Zinc**, highly reactive metals like **Aluminium** are themselves sometimes used as reducing agents in **thermite reactions** to extract metals like **Manganese (Mn)** or **Chromium (Cr)** from their oxides.
 
• **Electrolyte Purity:** For **electrolytic reduction**, the salt must be in a **molten (fused)** state or in a **solution** to allow the **ions** to move freely and conduct **electricity**.
</ul

questions.question: What is a reduction reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gain of electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **chemistry**, a **reduction reaction** is defined as a process where a **chemical species** (atom, ion, or molecule) **gains one or more electrons**.
 
• When an atom or ion gains electrons, its **oxidation state** or **oxidation number** decreases (becomes more negative or less positive). ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The process of **losing electrons** is known as **oxidation**, which is the exact opposite of reduction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Changes involving **neutrons** or **protons** are considered **nuclear reactions** rather than **chemical reactions**. **Loss of neutrons** usually occurs during **radioactive decay** or **nuclear fission**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Gain of protons** would change the **atomic number** of the element, essentially turning it into a different **chemical element** altogether, which does not happen in standard chemical reactions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A popular mnemonic to remember this is **OIL RIG**, which stands for **Oxidation Is Loss** (of electrons) and **Reduction Is Gain** (of electrons).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Redox Reactions:**
 
 
• Reduction and oxidation almost always occur simultaneously in a chemical process known as a **Redox reaction**.
 
• In these reactions, **electrons** are transferred from one substance to another. The substance that **loses electrons** is oxidized, and the substance that **gains electrons** is reduced.
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing and Reducing Agents:**
 
 
• A **reducing agent** (or reductant) is a substance that **donates electrons** to another substance, thereby undergoing **oxidation** itself.
 
• An **oxidizing agent** (or oxidant) is a substance that **accepts electrons** from another substance, thereby undergoing **reduction** itself.
 
 
 
• **Classical Definitions:**
 
 
• While the electronic definition is the most accurate, reduction was classically defined as the **loss of oxygen** or the **gain of hydrogen**.
 
• Conversely, oxidation was defined as the **gain of oxygen** or the **loss of hydrogen**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• In the **extraction of iron** from its ore (**Hematite - Fe2O3**), carbon monoxide acts as a reducing agent to remove oxygen from the iron oxide, leaving behind **metallic iron**.
 
• In **electroplating**, metal ions in a solution **gain electrons** at the **cathode** to form a solid metal coating on an object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Electrochemical Cells:** In a **battery** or galvanic cell, reduction always occurs at the **cathode**, while oxidation occurs at the **anode**.
 
• **Biological Significance:** Reduction reactions are vital in **photosynthesis** and **cellular respiration**. For instance, in photosynthesis, **carbon dioxide** is reduced to form **glucose**.
 
• **Oxidation Number Rules:**
 
 
• The oxidation number of a **free element** is always **zero**.
 
• For a **monatomic ion**, the oxidation number is equal to its **charge**.
 
• Oxygen usually has an oxidation number of **-2**, except in peroxides where it is **-1**.
 
• Hydrogen usually has an oxidation number of **+1** when bonded to non-metals and **-1** when bonded to metals.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A male patient has low sperm motility. Which glands are most likely to be NOT functioning properly?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prostate gland and seminal vesicles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **male reproductive system** consists of various organs and accessory glands that work together to produce, maintain, and transport sperm. **Sperm motility** refers to the ability of sperm to move efficiently.
 
• **Seminal Vesicles**: These are a pair of pouch-like glands located at the base of the urinary bladder. They secrete a thick, alkaline fluid that makes up approximately **60% to 70%** of the total volume of **semen**.
 
• The fluid from the **seminal vesicles** contains **fructose**, which provides the essential **energy source (ATP)** for sperm to swim. Without this energy, sperm remain immobile.
 
• **Prostate Gland**: This is a single, doughnut-shaped gland located just below the urinary bladder. It secretes a thin, milky, slightly alkaline fluid that contains **citrate**, **zinc**, and various **enzymes**.
 
• The secretions of the **prostate gland** play a crucial role in the **activation of sperm** and significantly enhance their **motility** and survival by neutralizing the acidic environment of the male urethra and the female reproductive tract.
 
• If a patient exhibits **low sperm motility** (a condition often termed **asthenozoospermia**), it indicates that the sperm lack the necessary biochemical environment or energy to move, pointing directly to the malfunction of the **prostate gland** and **seminal vesicles**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Prostate gland and seminal vesicles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Testis and Epididymis**:
 
 
• The **testes** are the primary reproductive organs responsible for the production of sperm (**spermatogenesis**) and the hormone **testosterone**.
 
• The **epididymis** is a coiled tube where sperm are stored and undergo **functional maturation**, gaining the potential for motility, although they only become fully active upon mixing with accessory gland secretions.
 
 
 
• **Bulbourethral Glands (Cowper's Glands)**:
 
 
• These are small glands located below the prostate. They secrete an alkaline mucus that **lubricates the urethra** and neutralizes any residual acidic urine before ejaculation.
 
 
 
• **Analysis of Incorrect Options**:
 
 
• **Pancreas and Adrenal Glands**: The **pancreas** regulates blood glucose levels via **insulin** and **glucagon**, while **adrenal glands** produce **adrenaline** and **cortisol** for stress response. Neither is directly responsible for sperm motility.
 
• **Thyroxine and Pineal Glands**: **Thyroxine** (produced by the thyroid) regulates **basal metabolic rate**, and the **pineal gland** produces **melatonin** to regulate the **circadian rhythm** (sleep-wake cycle).
 
• **Bladder**: The **urinary bladder** is part of the excretory system and serves only as a storage vessel for **urine**; it has no secretory role in sperm health.
 
 
 
• **Semen Composition**:
 
 
• **Semen** is a mixture of sperm and **seminal plasma**. The seminal plasma is formed by the combined secretions of the **seminal vesicles**, **prostate**, and **bulbourethral glands**, providing a transport medium, nutrients, and protection to the sperm cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fertilization Requirement**: For successful **fertilization**, sperm must travel from the vagina through the cervix and uterus to the fallopian tubes. This requires high **motility**, which is dependent on the chemical composition of the fluid provided by the accessory glands.
 
• **Hormonal Regulation**: The functioning of the **prostate** and **seminal vesicles** is maintained by the male sex hormone, **testosterone**, which is secreted by the **Leydig cells** in the testes under the influence of **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)**.

questions.question: Esters are ___________ substances.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweet-smelling**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Esters** are functional organic compounds derived from **carboxylic acids** and **alcohols**, characterized by a carbon atom double-bonded to an oxygen and single-bonded to an alkoxy group (**R-COOR'**).
 
• One of the most defining physical properties of low-molecular-weight esters is their pleasant, **fruity**, or **sweet-smelling** fragrance, which makes them highly distinguishable from the pungent odors of their parent acids.
 
• They are synthesized via a reaction called **esterification**, typically involving the heating of a **carboxylic acid** with an **alcohol** in the presence of a strong acid catalyst like **concentrated sulfuric acid** (H₂SO₄).
 
• In nature, esters are ubiquitous and are responsible for the natural **aroma** and **flavor** profiles of various fruits and flowers, such as **isoamyl acetate** (banana smell) and **ethyl butyrate** (pineapple smell).

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial and Commercial Uses**:
 
 
• Because of their **volatile nature** and pleasant scents, they are extensively used as **synthetic flavoring agents** in the food industry and as primary components in **perfumes** and **cosmetic products**.
 
• Esters like **ethyl acetate** are utilized as powerful **organic solvents** in nail polish removers, paints, and adhesives due to their ability to dissolve various organic substances.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Properties**:
 
 
• Under basic conditions, esters undergo a process called **saponification** (alkaline hydrolysis), which results in the formation of **soap** (salts of fatty acids) and an alcohol.
 
• Unlike carboxylic acids, esters are **neutral compounds** and do not react with **sodium bicarbonate** to release carbon dioxide, nor do they turn **blue litmus paper** red.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary safety function of the green insulated earth wire in a domestic circuit, particularly for metallic appliances?

options.text: To provide a high-resistance path to divert excess current into the ground
To stabilise the voltage at 220 V
To act as the neutral wire when the black wire fails
To provide a low-resistance path to ensure leakage current keeps the appliance potential to that of the earth, preventing severe shocks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide a low-resistance path to ensure leakage current keeps the appliance potential to that of the earth, preventing severe shocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **earth wire**, which typically has **green insulation**, is a vital **safety measure** in domestic electric circuits, especially for appliances with a **metallic body** like electric irons, toasters, and refrigerators.
 
• Its primary function is to provide a **low-resistance conducting path** for the electric current. If the insulation of the **live wire** inside an appliance fails and touches the metallic casing, the **earth wire** ensures that the current flows directly into the ground.
 
• By directing the **leakage current** to the earth, the wire maintains the **electric potential** of the appliance's metallic body at **zero volts** (the same as the earth), ensuring that a user touching the appliance does not receive a **severe electric shock**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **low-resistance path** is critical because electricity always follows the path of least resistance. Since the human body has higher resistance compared to the copper **earth wire**, the current prefers the wire over the person. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as it suggests a high-resistance path.***
 
• The earth wire does not regulate or **stabilize voltage**; voltage stabilization is the function of devices like **Voltage Stabilizers** or **Transformers**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **earth wire** is not designed to replace the **neutral wire**. While both are connected to the ground at some point in the power system, the neutral wire completes the circuit for normal operation, whereas the earth wire is strictly for **safety and protection**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Standard Color Coding:** In a typical domestic circuit in **India**, three types of wires are used. The **Live wire** (positive) usually has **red or brown insulation**, the **Neutral wire** (negative) has **black or blue insulation**, and the **Earth wire** has **green or yellow insulation**.
 
• **Domestic Power Supply:** In India, the **potential difference** (voltage) between the live and neutral wires is **220 V**, and the frequency of the alternating current (AC) is **50 Hz**.
 
• **Circuit Types:** Domestic circuits are often divided into two types: a **5 A current rating** circuit for low-power bulbs and fans, and a **15 A current rating** circuit for high-power appliances like air conditioners and geysers.
 
• **Safety Devices:** To prevent damage from **short-circuiting** or **overloading**, devices such as **Electric Fuses** and **Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCB)** are installed. A fuse works on the **heating effect of current** and breaks the circuit if the current exceeds a safe limit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Earthing Mechanism:** The **earth wire** is connected to a **metal plate** buried deep in the earth near the house. This setup ensures that any **excess charge** or leakage is instantly discharged into the ground.
 
• **Short Circuiting:** This occurs when the **live wire** and the **neutral wire** come into direct contact due to damaged insulation or a fault in the appliance, causing a sudden, massive surge in **current**.
 
• **Overloading:** This happens when too many high-power appliances are connected to a **single socket**, drawing more current than the wires can safely carry, leading to potential **fire hazards**.
 
• **Three-Pin Plugs:** The top pin of a **three-pin plug** is the **earth pin**. It is intentionally made **longer and thicker** than the live and neutral pins to ensure the appliance is grounded first before the power is connected.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following determine the size of an atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electron Clouds**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **size of an atom** is almost entirely determined by the volume of its **Electron Clouds**. Although electrons have negligible mass, they move rapidly in regions of space around the nucleus, creating a "cloud" that defines the atom's outer boundary.
 
• While the **nucleus** contains more than **99.9%** of the atom's total mass, it occupies an extremely small fraction of the atom's volume. If an atom were expanded to the size of a football stadium, the nucleus would be the size of a small **marble** in the center, while the **electron cloud** would fill the rest of the stadium.
 
• The **atomic radius** is the physical distance from the center of the nucleus to the outermost stable **electron orbital**. This radius typically ranges from **30 to 300 picometers (pm)** (1 picometer = **10^-12 meters**).
 
• The distribution of electrons in different **energy levels** (shells) and **subshells** (s, p, d, f orbitals) dictates how much space the atom takes up. Atoms with more **electron shells** are generally larger in size.
 
• The interaction between the **positively charged nucleus** and the **negatively charged electrons** determines how tightly the cloud is pulled inward, thus influencing the overall **atomic volume**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**:
 
 
• The **nucleus** was discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in **1911** through his famous **Gold Foil Experiment**.
 
• It is the dense, central core of the atom containing **protons** and **neutrons**. The diameter of a nucleus is about **10^-15 meters**, which is **100,000 times smaller** than the atom itself (**10^-10 meters**).
 
 
 
• **Protons and Neutrons**:
 
 
• **Protons** are positively charged particles discovered by **Ernest Rutherford**. The number of protons is known as the **Atomic Number (Z)** and determines the identity of the chemical element.
 
• **Neutrons** are neutral subatomic particles discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**. Together with protons, they make up the **Atomic Mass** of the atom but do not contribute to its volume.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Atomic Size**:
 
 
• In the **Periodic Table**, the atomic size **decreases** across a **period** (from left to right) because the increasing **nuclear charge** pulls the **electron cloud** closer to the center.
 
• The atomic size **increases** down a **group** (from top to bottom) because new **principal energy levels** or shells are added, which are further from the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Units**:
 
 
• Atomic sizes are often measured in **Angstroms (Å)** or **Nanometers (nm)**. One **Angstrom** is equal to **10^-10 meters**, which is roughly the size of a **hydrogen atom**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: According to Bohr-Bury, what is the maximum number of electrons that the M-shell can accommodate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distribution of electrons in different orbits or shells of an atom was suggested by **Bohr** and **Bury** in the year **1921**. According to this scheme, the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a shell is given by the formula **2n²**, where **'n'** is the **orbit number** or **energy level index**.
 
• The **M-shell** is the **third shell** from the nucleus of an atom, which means its principal quantum number or orbit number **n** is equal to **3**.
 
• By applying the **2n²** formula for the **M-shell**, the calculation is **2 x (3)²**, which equals **2 x 9 = 18**. Therefore, the **M-shell** can accommodate a maximum of **18 electrons**.
 
• This rule dictates the capacity of each discrete energy level. For the first three shells, the capacities are **K-shell (2)**, **L-shell (8)**, and **M-shell (18)**.
 
• While the **M-shell** has a physical capacity for **18 electrons**, the **Bohr-Bury scheme** also specifies that the **outermost shell** of any atom cannot accommodate more than **8 electrons**, even if it has the capacity for more.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **K-Shell (n=1):**
 
 
• The **K-shell** is the **first shell** and is closest to the **nucleus**.
 
• Using the formula **2(1)²**, its maximum capacity is **2 electrons**.
 
• Elements like **Hydrogen** and **Helium** fill this shell first.
 
 
 
• **L-Shell (n=2):**
 
 
• The **L-shell** is the **second shell**.
 
• Following the formula **2(2)²**, it can hold a maximum of **8 electrons**.
 
• Once the **K-shell** is full, electrons begin to occupy the **L-shell**.
 
 
 
• **N-Shell (n=4):**
 
 
• The **N-shell** is the **fourth shell** from the nucleus.
 
• According to the **2n²** rule, where **n=4**, the calculation is **2 x (4)² = 2 x 16**, resulting in a maximum of **32 electrons**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Bohr Model:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Neils Bohr** in **1913**, this model introduced the idea that **electrons** travel in **defined circular orbits** around the **nucleus**.
 
• The model explains that **energy** is absorbed or emitted only when an **electron** jumps from one **orbit** to another.
 
• The **Bohr-Bury scheme** refined this by providing the rules for **electron configuration** and **stability**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Octet Rule:** Regardless of the shell's maximum capacity (like 18 for M or 32 for N), the **outermost shell** (valence shell) is considered stable when it contains **8 electrons**. This is known as the **Octet Rule**.
 
• **Step-wise Filling:** Electrons are not accommodated in a given shell unless the **inner shells** are completely filled. This means the **shells are filled in a step-wise manner** starting from the lowest energy level (K) to higher ones.
 
• **Energy Levels:** As the value of **n** increases, the **energy** of the shell also **increases**, and the shell is located **farther** from the **nucleus**.
 
• **Valence Electrons:** The electrons present in the **outermost shell** are called **valence electrons**, and they determine the **chemical reactivity** and **valency** of the **element**.
</ul

questions.question: What can be said about the shape of a velocity-time graph for an object moving with non-uniform acceleration?

options.text: It is always a straight line.
It is always a downward sloping line.
It is always a horizontal line.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a curved line.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **velocity-time graph** (v-t graph) is a graphical representation used in **kinematics** to show how the **velocity** of an object changes with respect to **time**. The **y-axis** represents velocity, typically measured in **meters per second (m/s)**, and the **x-axis** represents time, measured in **seconds (s)**.
 
• The **slope** or **gradient** of a velocity-time graph represents the **acceleration** of the moving object. If the slope is **constant**, the acceleration is **uniform**; if the slope **varies**, the acceleration is **non-uniform**.
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration** occurs when the velocity of an object changes by **unequal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**. This implies that the rate of change of velocity is not a **constant value** throughout the motion.
 
• In the case of non-uniform acceleration, the **slope** of the graph changes at every point. Geometrically, a line with a continuously changing slope is represented as a **curved line**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• If the graph were a **straight line** (sloping upwards or downwards), it would represent **uniform acceleration** or **uniform retardation**, where the rate of change of velocity remains **fixed**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A **horizontal line** on a v-t graph indicates that the velocity is **constant** over time, meaning the acceleration is exactly **zero**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Motion on v-t Graphs**:
 
 
• **Uniform Velocity**: Represented by a **straight horizontal line** parallel to the **time axis**. The **acceleration** in this case is **0 m/s²**.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration**: Represented by a **straight line** with a **positive slope**. This means the object's velocity increases at a **steady rate**.
 
• **Uniform Retardation (Deceleration)**: Represented by a **straight line** with a **negative slope** (sloping downwards). The velocity decreases at a **constant rate**.
 
• **Non-uniform Acceleration**: Represented by **curves**. A curve bending **upwards** indicates **increasing acceleration**, while a curve leveling off indicates **decreasing acceleration**.
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Displacement**: One of the most important features of a velocity-time graph is that the **area under the curve** (between the line and the time axis) represents the total **displacement** covered by the object. For a curved graph, this area is often calculated using **integration** in **calculus**.
 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration**: In a non-uniform acceleration scenario, the **instantaneous acceleration** at any specific **time (t)** is found by calculating the **slope of the tangent** drawn to the **curved line** at that specific point.
 
• **Average Acceleration**: For an object moving with non-uniform acceleration between two time intervals, the **average acceleration** is calculated by finding the **change in velocity** divided by the **total time taken**, which corresponds to the slope of the **chord** connecting the two points on the curve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Physical Units**: Always remember that the **SI unit** for velocity is **m/s** and for acceleration is **m/s²**. On a graph, the **product** of the units of the two axes (m/s * s) yields the unit of **displacement**, which is **meters (m)**.
 
• **Non-Zero Intercept**: A velocity-time graph does not always have to start at the **origin (0,0)**. If it starts at a point on the y-axis, it indicates that the object had an **initial velocity (u)** at **time t = 0**.
 
• **Direction of Motion**: If the graph crosses below the **x-axis** into the **negative y-region**, it signifies that the object has **changed direction** and is moving in the **opposite direction** relative to the starting reference.

• Aerobic respiration 
• Does not require oxygen 
 
• Anaerobic respiration 
• Mitochondria 
 
• Pyruvate breakdown in the presence of oxygen takes place in the 
• Cytoplasm 
 
• Glucose breakdown in the absence of oxygen takes place in the 
• Requires oxygen <br/

options.text: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
a - iv, b - i, c - iii, d - ii
a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv
a - i, b - iv, c - ii, d - iii

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerobic respiration** is a biological process in which food glucose is converted into energy in the presence of **oxygen**. This type of respiration is common in most higher organisms, including humans, animals, and plants. ***Hence, statement a matches with iv.***
 
• **Anaerobic respiration** takes place in the **absence of oxygen**. In this process, the incomplete breakdown of food occurs, leading to the production of significantly less energy compared to aerobic respiration. Examples include **fermentation** in yeast and energy production in human muscles during heavy exercise. ***Hence, statement b matches with i.***
 
• During **aerobic respiration**, the **pyruvate** molecule (produced from glucose) enters the **Mitochondria**. Here, in the presence of **oxygen**, it is completely broken down into **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and a large amount of **ATP**. ***Hence, statement c matches with ii.***
 
• The first step of cellular respiration is **glycolysis**, which involves the breakdown of **glucose** (a **6-carbon** molecule) into **pyruvate** (a **3-carbon** molecule). This specific stage, as well as anaerobic pathways where oxygen is absent, occurs within the **Cytoplasm** of the **cell**. ***Hence, statement d matches with iii.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct matching sequence is a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Site of Respiration:** While **glycolysis** happens in the **cytoplasm**, the **Krebs cycle** and **electron transport chain** occur in the **mitochondria**. The **mitochondria** are often called the **powerhouse of the cell** because they generate the bulk of **ATP**.
 
• **Energy Yield:** **Aerobic respiration** is highly efficient, typically yielding approximately **36 to 38 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule. In contrast, **anaerobic respiration** produces only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
• **By-products:** In aerobic conditions, the by-products are **CO2** and **water**. In anaerobic conditions in humans, **lactic acid** is produced, which can cause muscle cramps. In **yeast**, the anaerobic process produces **ethanol** and **CO2**, a process widely used in the **brewing and baking industries**.
 
• **Role of Pyruvate:** **Pyruvate** acts as a crucial metabolic intermediate. Depending on the availability of **oxygen**, it either enters the **mitochondria** for further oxidation or undergoes **fermentation** in the **cytoplasm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate):** This is known as the **energy currency** of the cell. The energy released during **respiration** is used to synthesize **ATP** from **ADP** and inorganic phosphate.
 
• **Muscle Fatigue:** During vigorous exercise, when the supply of **oxygen** to our muscle cells is insufficient, **anaerobic respiration** takes place, leading to the accumulation of **lactic acid**. This accumulation is the primary cause of **muscle cramps** and fatigue.
 
• **Cellular Respiration stages:** It involves four main stages: **Glycolysis** (Cytoplasm), **Pyruvate Oxidation** (Mitochondria), **Citric Acid Cycle/Krebs Cycle** (Mitochondria), and **Oxidative Phosphorylation** (Mitochondria).
 
• **Universal Process:** **Glycolysis** is considered the most ancient metabolic pathway as it occurs in almost all living organisms, regardless of whether they breathe **oxygen** or not, and it always takes place in the **cytosol/cytoplasm**.
</ul

questions.question: Which among the following statements represents a characteristic of asexual reproduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involves only one parent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a biological process by which an organism creates a **genetically similar or identical copy** of itself without the contribution of genetic material from another individual.
 
• It **involves only one parent**, meaning there is no requirement for a partner or the **fusion of male and female gametes**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct and statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **offspring** produced through this method are **genetically identical** to the parent and are often referred to as **clones**. This process does not lead to **genetic diversity** within the population. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• This mode of reproduction does not typically **require gametes** (sperm and egg cells), nor does it involve **fertilization**. It relies primarily on **mitotic cell division**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• It is a **rapid and energy-efficient** method of multiplication, commonly found in **unicellular organisms**, **bacteria**, **archaea**, and many **plants** and **fungi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Asexual Reproduction:**
 
 
• **Binary Fission:** A **parent cell** divides into two equal **daughter cells**. This is common in **Amoeba** and **Bacteria**.
 
• **Budding:** A small **outgrowth or bud** develops on the parent body, which eventually detaches to become a new individual. Examples include **Yeast** and **Hydra**.
 
• **Fragmentation:** The body of the parent breaks into **distinct pieces**, and each piece grows into a complete organism. This is seen in **Spirogyra** and **Planaria**.
 
• **Spore Formation:** Organisms produce microscopic **reproductive units** called **spores** that germinate under favorable conditions. Example: **Rhizopus (Bread Mould)**.
 
 
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction in **plants** where new plants are produced from **vegetative parts** like **roots, stems, or leaves**.
 
• Examples include **Potato (tubers)**, **Ginger (rhizomes)**, and **Bryophyllum (leaf buds)**.
 
 
 
• **Sexual Reproduction Comparison:**
 
 
• In contrast, **sexual reproduction** involves **two parents** and the **fusion of haploid gametes** to form a **diploid zygote**, resulting in **genetic variation** which is crucial for **evolution** and **adaptation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages:** The population can be increased **rapidly** when conditions are favorable. Only **one parent** is needed, which is more **time and energy efficient** as it eliminates the need to find a **mate**.
 
• **Disadvantages:** It does not lead to **genetic variation** in a population. The species may only be suited to one **habitat**, and **disease** may affect all individuals in a population because they are all **genetically identical**.
 
• **Parthenogenesis:** This is a special form of asexual reproduction where an **unfertilized egg** develops into a new individual. This occurs in some **invertebrates** (like **bees** and **wasps**) and a few **vertebrates** (like certain **lizards**).
</ul
